title: Texas assumed name certificates for an LLC or a registered series
rule: A Texas LLC, or a registered series of one, that regularly does business in Texas under a name other than the one in its certificate of formation (for a series, its certificate of registered series) files an assumed name certificate with the Secretary of State, for $25. A protected series name lacking the LLC's name is also an assumed name of the LLC. A certificate lasts no more than 10 years and is void at the end of its term unless a renewal is filed in the six months before it expires. Until it files one, the entity cannot sue in Texas on a contract made under the assumed name.
changeWatch: Amendments to Business and Commerce Code chapter 71; the county-filing provisions for entities were repealed effective September 1, 2019.

sources.title: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 71, Assumed Business or Professional Name Act
sources.quote: A certificate is effective for a term not to exceed 10 years from the date the certificate is filed.
